problem: Part (c) gives the catheter path as 1 kΩ, but Section 1 states that an internal path from a catheter is a few hundred ohms (300 Ω to 500 Ω). A student meets two different values for the same path in one chapter.
fix: Use 500 Ω in part (c): I = 0.1 V / 500 Ω = 0.0002 A = 200 µA, which is twenty times the 10 µA target. Or state in Section 1 that a saline-filled catheter with its column of fluid can be about 1 kΩ and keep the example as it is.

problem: "The common design target for patient-connected equipment is 10 µA of leakage current" is too broad. In IEC 60601-1 the 10 µA patient-leakage limit applies to Type CF (intracardiac) applied parts; Type BF and Type B parts are allowed 100 µA in normal condition.
fix: Say: "The limit for an intracardiac (Type CF) connection is 10 µA of patient leakage current; general patient-connected parts are allowed about 100 µA." Then the later comparisons with the 10 µA target stay tied to the catheter case.

problem: "About a thousand times smaller" does not match "tens of microamps". At 20 µA the ratio to 100 mA is 5000, not 1000; only 100 µA gives a ratio of 1000, and 100 µA is not "tens of microamps".
fix: "The intracardiac danger level is a few tens of microamps, two to three orders of magnitude below the 100 mA macro-shock level." Or give one number: "20 µA is 5000 times smaller than 100 mA."
